content: The Founder stays standing, arms crossed, looking at the board rather than at Community. 'No face. That was never an accident. Preserve isn't about me. The day it's my face, it's a personal brand selling tins. The number on the tin is the identity. You're asking me to swap the thing that makes it collectible for the thing that makes it ordinary.'
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap
disagreement: Founder (stay faceless) vs Community (a visible human closes the trust gap)

content: Head of Product keeps their voice level. 'Let's separate the problem from the remedy. The problem has three parts: no face, no history, paying before the product exists. A face is one possible fix for one of the three. Let's put every fix up there, not just the face.'
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap

content: Research raises a cautious hand towards Community. 'For honesty: in the report, 6 of 28 cited trust, and they were mostly non-buyers. Whether a face would move real ones, nobody knows. I won't let the Founder's instinct or yours stand in for a test.'
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap

content: Brand, unexpectedly, leans halfway towards the Founder. 'Mystique is half of why the reel got watched. But faceless and anonymous aren't the same thing. Hands, the bench, the brush, the paint under someone's nails. That's a person without being a personal brand.'
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap

proposals.text: 'Hands, not face': process content showing the founder's hands painting tins at the bench, without showing his face
proposals.test: reel A/B: process/hands creative vs mystique-only creative, measured on waitlist signups

content: The Designer turns tin 001 slowly under the light, showing the brushstrokes on the side, and leaves it facing the Founder.
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap

content: The Plant Specialist thinks the honest germination time-lapse is also a trust fix. A seed tray doesn't need a face to look real. They keep it in reserve.
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap

content: Growth backs Community, with a funnel slant. 'Real buyers holding their numbers. Receipts with the personal details blurred. Unboxings. That's proof, and it's free content. In the report, the cautious collector literally said I'll preorder when the first buyers show up with receipts.'
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap

content: Community walks up to the board and stands next to the line they wrote, close enough that the Founder has to look at them. 'I'm not asking you to become an influencer. I'm saying someone paid Rs 1,099 to a page with no face, no history and no product. The collector lead only bought after you answered the reseller rumour in your own words. Your words were the proof. Imagine what your hands could do. Or a name on the terms. Or a real person answering DMs with a name.'
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap

proposals.text: A visible human: founder's face or at minimum a named person behind the brand on the terms and in support replies
proposals.cost: none in money; cost is to mystique

content: CX adds quietly: 'Even if you stay faceless, support can't. If I'm answering refund questions, I want to sign them with a name. Mine is fine.'
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap

proposals.text: Support replies signed by a named team member (CX Lead)
proposals.test: trust objections in DMs before vs after

content: Ops studies the floor. They've seen founders dig in before, and they're waiting to find out whether this one does.
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap

content: Finance thinks about the skeptic's maths and finds it isn't wrong. All the money arrives before anything exists. Whatever this room decides about faces, the preorder cap and the remedy promise are already doing some of the trust work.
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap

content: Legal speaks slowly and carefully. 'I'll stay out of the creative argument. But there's an accountability question separate from faces. Buyers paying in advance should be able to see who they're dealing with and how to reach them, for example a business name and a contact on the preorder terms. Proposal only. Verify with a professional what's actually required.'
round_time: After lunch, Day 2 - Pain point 4: the prepay trust gap

proposals.text: Name the business entity and a contact route on the preorder terms (accountability without a face)
proposals.cost: low (professional review fee may apply - flag)
proposals.test: professional review; trust objections in DMs
